messages.subject: Categorical Omega
parts:
Hello!

I am running a cfa(). I am interested in calculating Green and Yang's categorical omega, but (to be honest...) I am a little confused with the information available on the internet.

I tried to adapt the SAS code of the Green and Yang's article, but what I get was one coefficient for the entire scale (two factors). This was disappointing because, as far as I know, reliability rest on uni-dimensional assumption, that is, one coefficient per factor.

I would really appreciate any help. Thanks in advance.

messages.subject: Re: Categorical Omega
parts:
I am interested in calculating Green and Yang's categorical omega, but (to be honest...) I am a little confused with the information available on the internet.

I tried to adapt the SAS code of the Green and Yang's article

Were you aware it was available in the semTools package?  Install the development version:

remotes::install_github("simsem/semTools/semTools")

And look up the ?compRelSEM help page.  If you feed it a multidimensional CFA from lavaan, the default is to give you reliability of a composite calculated per factor (assuming that a composite is calculated by summing/averaging all its indicators).  

If you wanted an overall reliability of a single composite, calculated for a multidimensional construct (i.e., if you were to sum all indicators in your CFA), you would have to explicitly request that using the return.total=TRUE argument.

The argument ord.scale=TRUE (default) is to use Green & Yang's (2009) approach when all indicators are treated as ordered= by lavaan:cfa().
